full_parsed_record.title: The weighted bipartite-graph product conjecture
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $G$ be any graph and let $W$ be any collection of weights on $G$. For each $u\in V(G)$, let $\{n_1(u),\ldots,n_{d(u)}(u)\}$ be the set of neighbours of $u$. For each edge $uv\in E(G)$, label the degree-$d(u)$ vertices of $K_{d(u),d(v)}$ by $w_1(u,v),\ldots,w_{d(v)}(u,v)$ and the degree-$d(v)$ vertices by $z_1(u,v),\ldots,z_{d(u)}(u,v)$. Let $W^{uv}$ be the collection of weights on $K_{d(u),d(v)}$ given by

$$
\lambda^{u,v}_{i,w_j(u,v)}=\lambda_{i,n_j(v)},\qquad \lambda^{u,v}_{i,z_j(u,v)}=\lambda_{i,n_j(u)},\qquad \lambda^{u,v}_{ij,w_j(u,v)z_k(u,v)}=\lambda_{ij,n_j(v)n_k(u)}.
$$

**Weighted bipartite-graph product conjecture.** Then

$$
Z^W(G)\leq\prod_{uv\in E(G)}Z^{W^{uv}}(K_{d(u),d(v)})^{\frac{1}{d(u)d(v)}}.
$$

The conjecture is proposed as the weighted analogue of Kahn's independent-set conjecture and is presented as an extension of a preceding theorem. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
full_parsed_record.source_name: David Galvin, “Bounding the partition function of spin-systems”, arXiv:1206.3200 (2012).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.3200

full_parsed_record.title: Modified Nivat conjecture in terms of nonexpansive subspaces
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $\eta\in\mathcal{A}^{\mathbb{Z}^2}$, let $X_{\eta}:=\overline{\mathcal{O}(\eta)}$ be its translation orbit closure, and for a finite set $\mathcal{S}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^2$ define the discrepancy by

$$
D_{\eta}(\mathcal{S}):=P_{\eta}(\mathcal{S})-|\mathcal{S}|,
$$

where $P_{\eta}(\mathcal{S})$ is the number of distinct $\eta$-colorings of $\mathcal{S}$. A $1$-dimensional subspace is **nonexpansive** if it is not expansive for the translation action. **Modified Nivat conjecture.** If there exists an $n$ by $k$ rectangular subset $R\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^2$ satisfying

$$
D_{\eta}(R)\leq 0,
$$

then there is at most one nonexpansive $1$-dimensional subspace for the translation action on $X_{\eta}$. This is a reformulation using discrepancy rather than rectangular complexity; the paper leaves it open.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Van Cyr and Bryna Kra, “Nonexpansive Z^2 subdynamics and Nivat's conjecture”, arXiv:1208.4090 (2013).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1208.4090

full_parsed_record.title: Linear stability conjecture for unions of $t$-cosets in $S_n$
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A} subset S_n$, and let $t in \mathbb{N}$. Let $f$ denote the characteristic function of $\mathcal{A}$, and let $f_t$ denote the orthogonal projection of $f$ onto $U_t$. A **union of $t$-cosets** is a family formed by taking the union of cosets determined by fixing the images of $t$ points. **The conjecture.** If

$$
\mathbb{E}[(f-f_t)^2] \leq \epsilon \mathbb{E}[f],
$$

then there exists a family $\mathcal{B} subset S_n$ which is a union of $t$-cosets such that

$$
|\mathcal{A} \triangle \mathcal{B}| \leq C_0\epsilon |\mathcal{A}|,
$$

where $C_0$ is an absolute constant. The conjecture would give the common generalization of the paper's stability results, asserting linear dependence between the two relevant distances; the authors state that it should hold, but their techniques do not prove it.
full_parsed_record.source_name: David Ellis, Yuval Filmus and Ehud Friedgut, “A stability result for balanced dictatorships in S_n”, arXiv:1210.3989 (2017).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.3989

full_parsed_record.title: Wilmes' multiplicity conjecture for boundary divisors
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $G=(V,E)$ be an undirected, connected graph. Let $\beta_{k,D}$ be the refined Betti number of a divisor $D$, let $\operatorname{\mathcal{P}}_{k+1}$ be the set of partitions of $G$ into $k+1$ connected components, and let $\operatorname{B}(\Pi)/\operatorname{Img}\operatorname{L}$ denote the relevant boundary-divisor classes modulo the Laplacian image. Suppose that exactly $l$ distinct partitions $\Pi_j$ satisfy the displayed membership condition.

**Wilmes' multiplicity conjecture.** If there are exactly $l$ distinct partitions $\Pi_j\in\operatorname{\mathcal{P}}_{k+1}$ such that

$$
D\in\operatorname{B}(\Pi_j)/\operatorname{Img}\operatorname{L},
$$

then

$$
\beta_{k,D}=l.
$$

This conjecture refines the preceding support characterization by predicting that the refined Betti number records the number of partitions for which the divisor class is a boundary divisor. The source presents it as one of two general expected results; only the top-degree case is established in the supplied text, so the general statement remains open.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Horia Mania, “Wilmes' Conjecture and Boundary Divisors”, arXiv:1210.8109 (2012).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.8109

full_parsed_record.title: Currie–Saari recurrence conjecture for unbordered factors of the Thue–Morse sequence
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $\mathbf{t}=t_0t_1t_2\cdots$ be the Thue–Morse sequence, defined by $t_0=0$, $t_{2n}=t_n$, and $t_{2n+1}=1-t_n$ for $n\geq 0$. Let $f(n)$ denote the number of unbordered factors of length $n$ in $\mathbf{t}$. **Currie–Saari's conjecture.** The initial values are

$$
f(0)=1,\qquad f(1)=2,\qquad f(2)=2,
$$

and, for $n\geq 0$, $f$ satisfies

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(4n+1)&=f(2n+1),\\
f(8n+2)&=f(2n+1)-8f(4n)+f(4n+3)+4f(8n),\\
f(8n+3)&=2f(2n)-f(2n+1)+5f(4n)+f(4n+2)-3f(8n),\\
f(8n+4)&=-4f(4n)+2f(4n+2)+2f(8n),\\
f(8n+6)&=2f(2n)-f(2n+1)+f(4n)+f(4n+2)+f(4n+3)-f(8n),\\
f(16n)&=-2f(4n)+3f(8n),\\
f(16n+7)&=-2f(2n)+f(2n+1)-5f(4n)+f(4n+2)+3f(8n),\\
f(16n+8)&=-8f(4n)+4f(4n+2)+4f(8n),\\
f(16n+15)&=-8f(4n)+2f(4n+3)+4f(8n)+f(8n+7).
\end{aligned}
$$

The conjecture seeks an explicit description of the number of unbordered factors of each length; the preceding characterization determines which lengths occur but not their multiplicities. Its status is unresolved in the supplied source context.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Daniel Goc, Hamoon Mousavi and Jeffrey Shallit, “On the Number of Unbordered Factors”, arXiv:1211.1301 (2012).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.1301

full_parsed_record.title: The finite-quandle separation conjecture for knot symmetry classes
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $\mathcal G$ be the group generated by reversal and mirror operations on knots, and let $\mathcal K$ be a finite set of knots closed under the action of $\mathcal G$. For a finite sequence of finite quandles $\mathcal S=(Q_1,\ldots,Q_n)$, define

$$
C(K)=\bigl(\operatorname{Col}_{Q_1}(K),\operatorname{Col}_{Q_2}(K),\ldots,\operatorname{Col}_{Q_n}(K)\bigr).
$$

**Finite-quandle separation conjecture.** There exists such a sequence $\mathcal S$ satisfying, for all $K,K'\in\mathcal K$,

$$
C(K')=C(K)\quad\text{if and only if}\quad K'=K\text{ or }K'=mr(K).
$$

The weaker implication that equal coloring vectors force $\mathcal G(K')=\mathcal G(K)$ is also stated. The authors verify these claims computationally for various finite knot sets, including knots with at most 12 crossings, but the general finite-set assertion remains open.
full_parsed_record.source_name: W. Edwin Clark, Mohamed Elhamdadi, Masahico Saito and Timothy Yeatman, “Quandle Colorings of Knots and Applications”, arXiv:1312.3307 (2014).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1312.3307

full_parsed_record.title: Javadi–Maleki–Omoomi conjecture on local clique cover numbers
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\operatorname{lcc}(G)$ denote its local clique cover number. Let $\overline{G}$ be the complement of $G$. **Javadi–Maleki–Omoomi conjecture.** For every graph $G$ on $n$ vertices,

$$
\operatorname{lcc}(G)+\operatorname{lcc}(\overline{G})\leq n.
$$

This is a Nordhaus–Gaddum-type inequality for the local clique cover number. It was proposed by R. Javadi, Z. Maleki and B. Omoomi in 2012; the supplied source gives no resolution, so its status is open.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Csilla Bujtás, Akbar Davoodi, Ervin Győri and Zsolt Tuza, “Clique Coverings and Claw-free Graphs”, arXiv:1608.07686 (2016).

full_parsed_record.title: Neumann's arc-count conjecture for non-Desarguesian projective planes
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $\Pi$ be a finite projective plane of order $q$, and let $C_7(\Pi)$ denote its number of $7$-arcs. Write $C_7(q)$ for the corresponding value in the Desarguesian plane of order $q$.

**Neumann's arc-count conjecture.** The following equivalent inequalities should hold: for every finite non-Desarguesian plane,

$$
C_7(\Pi) < (q^2 + q + 1)(q^2 + q)q^2 (q-1)^2 (q - 3)(q - 5)(q^4 - 20q^3 + 148q^2 - 468q + 498),
$$

and, for every fixed odd prime power $q$ and every non-Desarguesian projective plane $\Pi$ of order $q$,

$$
C_7(\Pi) < C_7(q).
$$

These are reformulations of the conjecture that every non-Desarguesian finite projective plane contains a Fano subplane. The equivalence uses the source's theorem that $C_7(\Pi)+A_7(\Pi)$ depends only on $q$, together with the fact that Desarguesian planes of odd order contain no Fano subplanes. The source gives no resolution status.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Nathan Kaplan, Susie Kimport, Rachel Lawrence, Luke Peilen and Max Weinreich, “Counting Arcs in Projective Planes via Glynn's Algorithm”, arXiv:1612.05246 (2017).

full_parsed_record.title: The des-Wilf equivalence for two sets of West-2-stack-sortable patterns
full_parsed_record.statement:
For a permutation pattern $\tau$, let $F_n^{\operatorname{des}}(\tau;q)$ denote the descent generating polynomial over permutations in $\operatorname{Av}_n(\tau)$, and for sets of patterns let $F_n^{\operatorname{des}}(\Pi;q)$ be defined analogously. Write $\tau\equiv_{\operatorname{des}}\rho$ for equality of these polynomials for every $n$. **The des-Wilf equivalence conjecture.** The two sets of patterns satisfy

$$
\{2341,\,3241\}\equiv_{\operatorname{des}}\{2413,\,3142\}.
$$

The patterns in the left-hand set are the basis for the permutations that are West-$2$-stack-sortable, and the conjecture extends the paper's study of descent generating functions for avoidance classes. It is supported by the data considered in the paper, while no closed forms for the relevant functions are known.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Caden Bielawa, Robert Davis, Daniel Greeson and Qinhan Zhou, “Descents and des-Wilf Equivalence of Permutations Avoiding Certain Non-Classical Patterns”, arXiv:1706.06231 (2018).

full_parsed_record.title: Sagan–Savage major-index unimodality conjecture for 321-avoiding permutations
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let ${\mathcal{S}_n(321)}$ denote the set of permutations of length $n$ avoiding the pattern $321$, and let $\operatorname{maj}(\sigma)$ and $\operatorname{des}(\sigma)$ denote the major index and descent number of a permutation $\sigma$. For each $n$, write

$$
\sum_{\sigma \in {\mathcal{S}_n(321)}} q^{\operatorname{maj}(\sigma)}t^{\operatorname{des}(\sigma)}=\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor}A_{n,i}(q)t^i.
$$

**Sagan–Savage conjecture.** For all $n$ and $i$, the polynomial $A_{n,i}(q)$ is unimodal.

This conjecture asserts that, among 321-avoiding permutations of length $n$ with a fixed number of descents, the major index is distributed unimodally. The paper gives a formula for these polynomials and proves unimodality in the case of two descents, but the full conjecture remains open in the source.
full_parsed_record.source_name: William J. Keith, “Major index over descent for pattern-avoiding permutations”, arXiv:1707.01200 (2017).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.01200

full_parsed_record.title: Linear equivalence conjecture for hereditary and rooted quasirandomness
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph, let $p\in[0,1]$, and let $G$ be a graph. The property $\mathcal{P}_{H,p}^{*}(\delta)$ means that every $U\subseteq V(G)$ satisfies

$$
c(H,G[U])=p^{e(H)}|U|^{v(H)}\pm\delta v(G)^{v(H)}.
$$

Let $\mathcal{R}_{H,p}(\varepsilon)$ denote the rooted quasirandomness condition defined in the paper, requiring the appropriate labelled-copy estimates for vertex subsets associated with the vertices of $H$. **Linear equivalence conjecture.** For every graph $H$, every $p\in[0,1]$, and every $\delta>0$,

$$
\mathcal{P}_{H,p}^{*}(\delta)\implies\mathcal{R}_{H,p}(\varepsilon)
$$

for some $\varepsilon=O_{H,p}(\delta)$. The paper states that this conjecture remains open and that, together with its main theorem, it would suffice to establish linear equivalence between $\mathcal{P}_{H,p}^{*}(\varepsilon)$ and $\mathcal{R}_{H,p}(\varepsilon)$.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Xiaoyu He, “Linear dependence between hereditary quasirandomness conditions”, arXiv:1707.05396 (2018).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.05396

full_parsed_record.title: Dousse–Kim unimodality conjecture for overpartitions in a box
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $M,N$ be fixed nonnegative integers, and let $p_{M \times N}(t_1,\dots,t_k;n)$ denote the number of $(k,1)$-colored partitions of $n$ in an $M \times N$ box, with $t_i$ part sizes of color $i$. For fixed $n$, consider the coefficient of $q^n$ in the generating function

$$
\sum_{n,\vec{t}} p_{M \times N}(t_1,\dots,t_k;n) x_1^{t_1} \dots x_k^{t_k} q^n.
$$

Fix $n$ and set any one variable $x_i=1$, leaving an $(n-1)$-dimensional array of coefficients in the remaining variables $x_j$.

**Dousse–Kim's unimodality conjecture.** Any linear cut through this array is a unimodal sequence.

This generalizes the unimodality conjecture of Dousse and Kim for overpartitions in an $M \times N$ box. The related one-variable formulation asserts that, for fixed $n$, the coefficient of $q^n$ in

$$
\sum_{k=0}^{\min(M,N)} t^k q^{\binom{k+1}{2}} \left[ { M \atop k} \right]_q \left[ {{M+N-k} \atop N-k} \right]_q
$$

is unimodal in $t$; the multidimensional formulation remains open.
full_parsed_record.source_name: William J. Keith, “Restricted k-color partitions, II”, arXiv:2001.08351 (2020).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.08351

full_parsed_record.title: Termination conjecture for the pentagon contact representation algorithm
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $G$ be an inner triangulation of a $5$-gon, and let $F$ be an initial five color forest of $G$. The algorithm described above produces iterates for these data.

**Termination conjecture.** The algorithm terminates with a non-negative solution for every graph $G$ which is an inner triangulation of a $5$-gon, and for every initial five color forest $F$ of $G$.

The conjecture asserts termination and success of the algorithm for all admissible inputs. The paper reports that two independent implementations and experiments have always been successful, but the authors cannot prove that the iterations make progress and note that the algorithm might otherwise cycle forever.

full_parsed_record.title: Bryson–Ono–Pitman–Rhoades mod 4 conjectures for strongly unimodal sequences
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $u(n)$ count strongly unimodal sequences of size $n$, let $u(m,n)$ count those of rank $m$, and let $u(a,b;n)$ count those whose rank is congruent to $a$ modulo $b$. For a prime $\ell$ with $\ell\text{ congruent to }7,11,13,17\pmod{24}$ and satisfying the quadratic-character condition $\left(\frac{k}{\ell}\right)=-1$, set

$$
s(\ell)=\frac{\ell^2-1}{24}.
$$

**Bryson–Ono–Pitman–Rhoades conjecture.** For all $n$,

$$
u(\ell^2n+k\ell-s(\ell))\equiv0\pmod4.
$$

Moreover, for every $a\in\{0,1,2,3\}$,

$$
u(a,4;\ell^2n+k\ell-s(\ell))\equiv0\pmod2,
$$

and

$$
u(0,4;\ell^2n+k\ell-s(\ell))\equiv u(2,4;\ell^2n+k\ell-s(\ell))\pmod4.
$$

These congruences concern the rank distribution of strongly unimodal sequences and were conjectured as mod $4$ refinements of known parity results. The paper proves these conjectures.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Rong Chen and Frank Garvan, “A proof of the mod 4 unimodal sequence conjectures and related mock theta functions”, arXiv:2010.14315 (2020).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.14315

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of October 2020). “This conjecture is false.”

full_parsed_record.title: Conjectured Laplacian coefficient bounds for graphs via closed walks
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with adjacency matrix $A=A(G)$, and let $A_1=A(L_1(G))$ be the adjacency matrix of its line graph. Write $c_{n-k}(G)$ for the corresponding Laplacian coefficient, and let the girth of $G$ be the length of its shortest cycle. **Laplacian coefficient bounds conjecture.** The following inequalities and equality conditions are conjectured:

1. 
$$
c_{n-4}(G)\leq \frac{1}{4!}\Big[\prod_{i=0}^3\big(\operatorname{tr} A^2-2i\big)-6(\operatorname{tr} A^2)^2\operatorname{tr} A_1^2+\operatorname{tr} A^2\operatorname{tr}(60A_1^2+8A_1^3)-\operatorname{tr}(144A_1^2+48A_1^3+6A_1^4)+3(\operatorname{tr} A_1^2)^2\Big],
$$

with equality if and only if the girth of $G$ is not $3$.

2. 
$$
c_{n-5}(G)\leq \frac{1}{5!}\Big[\prod_{i=0}^4\big(\operatorname{tr} A^2-2i\big)-10(\operatorname{tr} A^2)^3\operatorname{tr} A_1^2+(\operatorname{tr} A^2)^2\operatorname{tr}(180A_1^2+20A_1^3)-\operatorname{tr} A^2\operatorname{tr}(1040A_1^2+280A_1^3+30A_1^4)+15\operatorname{tr} A^2(\operatorname{tr} A_1^2)^2-\operatorname{tr} A_1^2\operatorname{tr}(120A_1^2+20A_1^3)+\operatorname{tr}(1920A_1^2+960A_1^3+240A_1^4+24A_1^5)\Big],
$$

with equality if and only if the girth of $G$ is not $3$ or $5$.

3. 
$$
c_{n-6}(G)\leq \frac{1}{6!}\Big[\prod_{i=0}^5\big(\operatorname{tr} A^2-2i\big)-15(\operatorname{tr} A^2)^4\operatorname{tr} A_1^2+(\operatorname{tr} A^2)^3\operatorname{tr}(420A_1^2+40A_1^3)-(\operatorname{tr} A^2)^2\operatorname{tr}(4260A_1^2+960A_1^3+90A_1^4)+45(\operatorname{tr} A^2\operatorname{tr} A_1^2)^2-810\operatorname{tr} A^2(\operatorname{tr} A_1^2)^2+\operatorname{tr} A^2\operatorname{tr}(18480A_1^2+7520A_1^3+1620A_1^4+144A_1^5)-15(\operatorname{tr} A_1^2)^3+3600(\operatorname{tr} A_1^2)^2-28800\operatorname{tr} A_1^2+\operatorname{tr} A_1^2\operatorname{tr}(1200A_1^3+90A_1^4)+40(\operatorname{tr} A_1^3)^2-120\operatorname{tr} A^2\operatorname{tr} A_1^2\operatorname{tr} A_1^3-\operatorname{tr}(19200A_1^3-7200A_1^4-1440A_1^5-120A_1^6)\Big],
$$

with equality if and only if the girth of $G$ is not $3$ or $5$.

These conjectured formulas extend the paper's exact expression for $c_{n-6}$ and earlier formulas for lower-index Laplacian coefficients, expressing them through traces that count closed walks in $G$ and its line graph. The supplied text does not indicate whether the conjecture has been resolved.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Ali Ghalavand and Ali Reza Ashrafi, “Laplacian Coefficients of a Forest in terms of the Number of Closed Walks in the Forest and its Line Graph”, arXiv:2104.08476 (2021).
full_parsed_record.references:

full_parsed_record.title: The short zero-sum sequence structure conjecture for rank-two abelian groups
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $n\geq 2$ and $m\geq 1$, let $G=C_n\oplus C_{mn}$, let $k\in [0,n-1]$, and let $S$ be a sequence of terms from $G$ with

$$
|S|=mn+n-2+k\quad\text{and}\quad 0\notin \Sigma_{\leq mn+n-1-k}(S).
$$

Here $C_r$ denotes the cyclic group of order $r$, $\Sigma_{\leq t}(S)$ is the set of sums of nonempty subsequences of $S$ of length at most $t$, and $\sigma(S)$ is the sum of all terms of $S$. A sequence is written multiplicatively, with $g^{[r]}$ denoting $r$ copies of $g$ and $\prod^{\bullet}$ denoting a sequence product. A basis $(e_1,e_2)$ is a basis of $G$, and a generating set $\{g_1,g_2\}$ generates $G$.

**Short zero-sum sequence structure conjecture.** There exists either a basis $(e_1,e_2)$ for $G$ with $\operatorname{ord}(e_2)=mn$ or a generating set $\{g_1,g_2\}$ for $G$ with $\operatorname{ord}(g_1+g_2)=mn$ such that the following hold: if $k=0$, then $S\boldsymbol{\cdot} g$ satisfies one of the possibilities given in Item 2, where $g=-\sigma(S)$; if $k=1$, then one of Items 2(a)--(d) holds; if $k\in [2,n-2]$, then either

$$
S=e_1^{[n-1]}\boldsymbol{\cdot}e_2^{[sn-1]}\boldsymbol{\cdot}(e_1+e_2)^{[(m-s)n+k]}
$$

for some $s\in [1,m]$, or

$$
S=g_1^{[n-1]}\boldsymbol{\cdot}g_2^{[n-1]}\boldsymbol{\cdot}(g_1+g_2)^{[(m-1)n+k]};
$$

if $k=n-1$, then either

$$
S=e_1^{[n-1]}\boldsymbol{\cdot}e_2^{[sn-1]}\boldsymbol{\cdot}(xe_1+e_2)^{[(m-s)n+n-1]}
$$

for some $s\in [1,m]$ and $x\in [1,n-1]$ with $\gcd(x,n)=1$, or

$$
S=g_1^{[n-1]}\boldsymbol{\cdot}g_2^{[n-1]}\boldsymbol{\cdot}(g_1+g_2)^{[(m-1)n+n-1]}.
$$

Moreover, if $m=1$, then the first alternative in each applicable part holds.

This conjecture would characterize all extremal sequences for the zero-sum invariant $\mathsf{s}_{\leq mn+n-1-k}(G)$ over rank-two groups $C_n\oplus C_{mn}$. Parts 1, 2 and 4 are stated as known in the source, while Part 3 is known for $m=1$, prime $n=p$, and $k\leq (2p+1)/3$; the general characterization remains open.
full_parsed_record.source_name: David J. Grynkiewicz and Chao Liu, “A Multiplicative Property for Zero-Sums II”, arXiv:2109.10309 (2021).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.10309

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).

full_parsed_record.title: Finite-convergence conjecture for the copositive stability-number hierarchy
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $M_G$ be its graph matrix, let $F_G(x)=(x^{\circ2})^TM_Gx^{\circ2}$, and let

$$
\mathcal K_n^{(r)}=\{M\in\mathcal S^n:(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2)^r(x^{\circ2})^TMx^{\circ2}\in\Sigma\}.
$$

Define $\vartheta^{(r)}(G)=\min\{t:t(A_G+I)-J\in\mathcal K_n^{(r)}\}$. The **finite-convergence conjecture.** For every graph $G$, there exists $r\in\mathbb N$ such that $M_G\in\mathcal K_n^{(r)}$, equivalently $(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2)^rF_G\in\Sigma$, equivalently $\vartheta^{(r)}(G)=\alpha(G)$, or equivalently $\vartheta\text{-rank}(G)<\infty$. This weaker conjecture asks only for finite convergence at some order and is explicitly stated to remain open.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Monique Laurent and Luis Felipe Vargas, “Exactness of Parrilo's conic approximations for copositive matrices and associated low order bounds for the stability number of a graph”, arXiv:2109.12876 (2021).

full_parsed_record.title: The lower-bound conjecture for secure domination in subdivisions
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let $G^{\frac{1}{2}}$ denote its $2$-subdivision, obtained by replacing each edge with a path of length $2$. Write $\gamma_s(H)$ for the secure domination number of a graph $H$.

**Secure-domination lower-bound conjecture.** For every graph $G$,

$$
\gamma_s\left(G^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)>\frac{4}{5}|V(G)|.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by examples showing that the secure domination number of a $2$-subdivision can be smaller than both the number of edges and the number of vertices of the original graph; its status is not established in the supplied source.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Nima Ghanbari, “Secure domination number of k-subdivision of graphs”, arXiv:2110.09190 (2023).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.09190

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2021).

full_parsed_record.title: Defective list edge-colouring conjecture
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and let $d$ be an integer. Write $ch'_d(G)$ for the $d$-defective list chromatic index and $\chi'_d(G)$ for the $d$-defective edge chromatic number.

**Defective list edge-colouring conjecture.** For every graph $G$ and every integer $d$,

$$
ch'_d(G)=\chi'_d(G).
$$

This is a stronger defective analogue of the list edge-colouring conjecture; the source says it is proved for bipartite graphs, while the general assertion remains open.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Pierre Aboulker, Guillaume Aubian and Chien-Chung Huang, “Vizing's and Shannon's Theorems for defective edge colouring”, arXiv:2201.11548 (2022).
full_parsed_record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1708.02370](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.02370), [arXiv:1611.09060](https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.09060).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.11548

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2022).

full_parsed_record.title: Henning–Klavžar–Rall 3/4-conjecture for the total domination game
full_parsed_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph without isolated vertices or edges, let $n=|V(G)|$, and let $\gamma_{tg}(G)$ denote the game total domination number of $G$, the number of selected vertices when Dominator starts and both players play optimally. **Henning–Klavžar–Rall's 3/4-conjecture.** For every such graph $G$,

$$
\gamma_{tg}(G) \leq \frac{3}{4}n.
$$

The conjecture is proved in the source paper, which establishes the bound for every graph without isolated vertices or edges.
full_parsed_record.source_name: Julien Portier and Leo Versteegen, “A proof of the 3/4 conjecture for the total domination game”, arXiv:2211.16432 (2022).
full_parsed_record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.16432

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of November 2022); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)
